study_identification_part.si4_title: Individual-level deviations from normative brain morphology in violence, psychosis, and psychopathy

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To assess the potential of normative modeling in forensic psychiatry neuroimaging research by investigating individual patterns of deviations from the norm in persons with a history of severe violence and schizophrenia spectrum disorder (SSD-V), in persons with a schizophrenia spectrum disorder but no history of violence (SSD-NV), persons with a history of severe violence without schizophrenia spectrum disorder (nonSSD-V), and healthy controls with no history of violence (HC).

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.answer: Freesurfer v7.1; Destrieux atlas; probabilistic atlas for subcortical segmentation
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The 'Quality control and preprocessing' section explicitly mentions the software, version, and atlases used.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: Freesurfer v7.1 was used to process data that passed quality control. Cortical thickness and area was summarized using the Destrieux atlas parcellation scheme [43]. Subcortical volume segmentation was based on a probabilistic atlas with priors for 31 brain structures [44, 45].

rci8_quality_checking.detail: Automated QC with MRIqc, followed by visual inspection by two raters. Exclusion based on visual inspection of cortical maps for negative values, unusual patterns, or hemispheric imbalance. 52 males and 20 females excluded for poor T1w quality, and 3 additional male individuals were excluded due to spurious abnormal brain findings.

Then two trained raters visually examined the scans marked for exclusion by MRIqc pipeline (NT and JR). ... caa6_deviation_metric.answer: Z-score. Extreme deviations defined as Z > 2 or Z < -2.
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: The statistical analysis section clearly defines the deviation metric and the threshold for extreme deviations.
caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: To summarize inter-individual variation within each group (SSD-V, SSD-NV, nonSSD-V and HC), we computed deviation scores (Z-scores) by separating them into positive and negative deviations. The percentage of subjects within each group with extreme positive (Z > 2) and negative (Z < -2) deviations at a given ROI were compared and reported [20].

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group comparisons of deviation scores were performed using General Linear Models (GLM) with permutation testing (PALM), controlling for age and ICV, with FWE correction. Group differences in the frequency of extreme deviations were tested with permutations. Associations between PCL-R scores and deviation scores were tested using GLM with permutations.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: By applying normative modeling, the study demonstrates heterogeneous patterns of brain morphometry deviations associated with violence and psychosis, which has the potential to improve understanding and inform clinical practice in forensic psychiatry.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The study found heterogeneous patterns of individual brain deviations, most prominent in the collateral transverse sulcus, lingual gyrus, and cerebellum for the SSD-V group. This pattern differed from the SSD-NV group (parieto-occipital and suborbital sulci) and the nonSSD-V group (paracentral and middle frontal regions). No significant associations were found between brain deviations and psychopathy traits after correction for multiple comparisons.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Limitations include the small sample size of violent groups, the male-only sample, lack of correction for substance use and antipsychotic medication effects, exclusion of the most severe cases, a binary definition of violence, and the cross-sectional design which cannot disentangle disease mechanisms from developmental influences.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: The study has some limitations. The relatively small number of subjects with a history of violence, as well as the male only sample... might limit the generalizability... the models were not corrected for substance use... we did not control for cumulative effects of antipsychotic medication... The most severely ill or aggressive persons... were not eligible... Violence was de /uniFB01 ned as a lifetime binary variable... an inherent limitation in all crosssectional neuroimaging studies is the inability to distinguish between speci /uniFB01 c disease mechanisms and the effects of early-life in /uniFB02 uences and developmental trajectories.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study provides a practical demonstration of how normative modeling can be applied to map heterogeneous, individual-level brain deviations in complex forensic psychiatric populations, moving beyond traditional case-control comparisons.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The study is notable for its application of pre-trained normative models to a unique and complex forensic psychiatric population. A large, separate healthy control sample (n=998) was used for fine-tuning/calibrating the model to the local scanners, which is a robust approach. The participant data is aggregated from four different ongoing studies (TOP, uTOP, STROKEMRI, sTOP). The supplementary material file (41398_2025_3343_MOESM1_ESM.pdf.md) was consulted and contains supplementary tables and figures referenced in the main text.
